turns.prompt_text: I would like to turn a table of links into a table where each element is a clickable "link" that takes the user to the link
turns.response_html:
To turn a plain list or table of URLs into functional, clickable hyperlinks, the method depends entirely on the tool you are using. Below are the most common ways to achieve this across different platforms.

1. Microsoft Excel & Google Sheets

If you have a column of URLs that are currently just plain text, you can convert them using a formula.

  • The Formula: Use the HYPERLINK function.

    =HYPERLINK(A1, "Click Here")

  • Bulk Conversion: If you want the clickable link to just show the URL itself, use:

    =HYPERLINK(A1, A1)

  • Quick Tip: In most spreadsheet apps, simply selecting a cell with a URL and pressing Enter or Space at the end of the text will auto-convert it into a clickable link.

2. HTML (For Web Pages)

If you are building a table for a website, you must wrap the URL inside an anchor tag (<a>).

Plain TextClickable HTML Code
https://google.com<a href="https://google.com">Visit Google</a>

Example Table Structure:

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Site Name</th>
    <th>Link</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Google</td>
    <td><a href="https://google.com">Go to Google</a></td>
  </tr>
</table>

3. Markdown (For GitHub, Notion, or Reddit)

Markdown is the simplest way to format links if you are using a modern documentation tool or notepad.

  • Syntax: [Link Text](URL)
  • In a Table:
| Service | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| Search Engine | [Click to Search](https://google.com) |
| Documentation | [View Docs](https://example.com) |

4. Microsoft Word

If your table is in a Word document:

  1. Highlight the text you want to turn into a link.
  2. Right-click and select Link (or press Ctrl + K).
  3. Paste the URL into the Address box and hit OK.
  4. Auto-Format: You can also go to File > Options > Proofing > AutoCorrect Options > AutoFormat As You Type and ensure "Internet and network paths with hyperlinks" is checked.

turns.prompt_text: In Google Sheets I'd like to chipify the entire table
turns.response_html:
To "chipify" a table in Google Sheets—turning plain URLs into those sleek, interactive Smart Chips—you can use the built-in Data Conversion tool. This is much cleaner than using formulas because it replaces the text directly with a functional object.

Here is the most efficient way to do it for an entire table:

The "Convert to Link Chip" Method

This is the fastest way to transform a range of existing URLs into Chips.

  1. Highlight the range of cells containing your links.
  2. Right-click anywhere in the highlighted area.
  3. Select Smart chips > Convert to link chip.
  4. Google Sheets will automatically fetch the metadata (like the website title and favicon) and replace the raw URL with a chip.

Handling Different Types of Data

If your table contains more than just website links (like email addresses or file paths), you can use specific chip types to make the table even more functional:

Data TypeChip Result
Email AddressesPeople Chips: Hovering shows contact info and "Send Email" buttons.
Google Drive LinksFile Chips: Shows the file name and allows for a quick preview.
Calendar LinksEvent Chips: Shows meeting times and attendee lists.
Google Maps LinksPlace Chips: Shows a mini-map and provides directions.

Pro Tip: Bulk "Insert" via Insert Menu

If you are starting from scratch or want to convert a specific column using the top menu:

  1. Go to the Insert menu at the top.
  2. Select Smart chips.
  3. Choose the specific category (e.g., People, Files, or Calendar events) if the "Link Chip" isn't providing the specific look you want.

Note: For the "Convert to link chip" option to work effectively, the text must be a valid, full URL (starting with http:// or https://).
